catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extracted from repository skeleton and symbol-level evidence. Code content was not fully inspected; patterns inferred from file structure and exposed symbols.
analysis_limits: Only symbol names and file paths were available; no function bodies or class implementations were inspected.
Pattern identification relies on naming conventions and structural decomposition, not on runtime behavior.
Agentic patterns (LLM control, agent roles) were excluded as per constraints.

system_map.overview: CAS Runner is a CLI-based tool for continuous architecture governance. It integrates with LLM providers, manages a knowledge base (cas-knowledge), enforces governance rules, and provides dashboards. The system is organized into distinct packages for governance, LLM client handling, dashboard health, and skills, with a central runner coordinating execution.

layers.name: Presentation
layers.purpose: CLI entry point and dashboard views

dependencies: CLI depends on Runner and Dashboard
Runner depends on Governance and LLM clients
LLM clients are independent and exchangeable

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: The governance domain is represented using Pydantic models, providing validation, serialization, and clarity for domain entities.
patterns.intent: To ensure type safety and validation for domain objects that carry governance data (e.g., inventories, risks, actions).
patterns.context: The system needs to manipulate complex governance structures (Resolutions, Metrics, Actions) while maintaining data integrity and clear boundaries.
forces: Data integrity is critical for governance decisions.
Models must be easily serializable for storage and exchange.
Domain concepts should map directly to code constructs.
patterns.solution: Define domain entities as Pydantic models, such as GovernanceInventory, GovernanceHealth, ComplianceFinding, and GovernanceAction, which enforce required fields and types.
implementation_signals: Multiple model classes with descriptive names ending in -Result, -Metrics, -Finding

failure_modes: If models become too large, they can become god objects.

patterns.reuse_notes: Can be reused for any domain object requiring validation; promotes a single source of truth for schemas.

patterns.name: Transition Registry for State Management
patterns.summary: The governance action engine uses a registry of allowed state transitions to drive workflow execution.
patterns.intent: To centralize and manage the legal set of state changes within governance processes.
patterns.context: Governance actions need to transition between states (e.g., proposed, approved, rejected) in a controlled manner.
forces: State transitions should be explicit and traceable
Need to enforce business rules on transitions
Should allow future extension with new states
patterns.solution: Implement a TransitionRegistry that holds valid transitions and is used by GovernanceActionEngine to validate and execute state changes.
implementation_signals: Registry likely contains mapping of source->target states

benefits: Rules are concentrated in one place
costs: May add complexity for simple state changes
Registry needs to be maintained manually
failure_modes: Registry can become stale if new states are added without updating it.

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful in any domain with well-defined lifecycle states.

patterns.name: LLM Provider Strategy
patterns.summary: The LLM interaction layer is abstracted behind a client interface, with two concrete implementations: one real (LiteLLM) and one mock.
patterns.intent: To decouple core orchestration from specific LLM vendors and enable testing.
patterns.context: The system needs to interact with LLMs for various tasks, but the actual provider may vary or be mocked in tests.
forces: Provider details should not leak into domain logic
Testing should not incur LLM costs or latency
Future providers should be easy to add
patterns.solution: Define a common interface (implicitly) and provide LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient implementations, allowing dynamic selection.
implementation_signals: Both clients reside in llm/ directory
MockLLMClient suggests a testing or fallback strategy
Likely share a common method signature

costs: Requires a defined interface to be effective
failure_modes: If interface is too generic, it may not capture provider-specific capabilities.

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply whenever an external service can be swapped or need to mock.

patterns.name: Layered Package Structure
patterns.summary: The source code is organized into packages that mirror architectural layers: governance, llm, dashboard, skills.
patterns.intent: To enforce separation of concerns and facilitate maintainability.
patterns.context: As the tool grows, it faces multiple cross-cutting concerns (governance, LLM integration, health dashboards) that need clear boundaries.
forces: Avoid mixing infrastructure with domain logic
Support independent evolution of modules
Allow easy onboarding of new developers
patterns.solution: Group related classes and modules into named packages (governance, llm, dashboard, skills) under src/cas_runner/.
implementation_signals: Directory src/cas_runner/governance/ exists with multiple modules
Dashboard and skills have their own modules

failure_modes: If dependencies cross layers improperly, architecture erosion occurs.

patterns.reuse_notes: This pattern is fundamental for any non-trivial application.

patterns.name: Bootstrap Configuration Setup
patterns.summary: The system has a bootstrap module that initializes workspace and merges configuration blocks for different agent frameworks.
patterns.intent: To provide a reproducible setup process that configures the environment consistently.
patterns.context: Running the CAS runner requires workspace initialization and synchronization of configuration files (like CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings).
forces: Users need a one-command setup
Configuration can vary across environments
Must not overwrite user's existing settings inadvertently
patterns.solution: Implement functions in bootstrap.py to merge governance blocks into configuration files and create symlinks or copies for necessary files.

costs: Potential for stale configuration if merges are not idempotent
failure_modes: If merging is too aggressive, it may clash with user customizations.

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any CLI tool that needs a bootstrap phase.

patterns.name: Compliance Rule Engine
patterns.summary: A dedicated engine (ComplianceEngine) centralizes rule evaluation and compliance checks across governance artifacts.
patterns.intent: To keep compliance logic separate from other components and allow systematic enforcement.
patterns.context: The system must validate that governance artifacts adhere to defined rules (e.g., architectural guidelines).
forces: Rules may change over time
Compliance checks should be repeatable and testable
Avoid scattering rule logic across codebase
patterns.solution: Implement ComplianceEngine that takes inventory of governance items and outputs ComplianceMetrics and ComplianceFinding objects.
implementation_signals: Output types like ComplianceFinding and ComplianceMetrics from models.py

costs: May become a performance bottleneck if rules are complex
Requires careful design of rule abstraction
failure_modes: Engine can become a god class if too many rules are added.

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable in domains with regulatory or policy checks.

patterns.name: Health Metrics Dashboard
patterns.summary: The dashboard module calculates and exposes system health status via a dedicated health model.
patterns.intent: To provide a simple, aggregated view of system health for operational monitoring.
patterns.context: Operators need a quick indicator of whether the CAS environment is healthy.
forces: Health status should be computed from multiple factors
Should be easy to extend with new health indicators
Output should be readable both for humans and machines
patterns.solution: Define HealthStatus enum and functions calculate_health and get_health_reasons to aggregate health data.

benefits: Potential for integration with monitoring tools
costs: Lacks detail if not structured well
failure_modes: If health calculation logic is ad-hoc, it may become inconsistent.

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful for any system that needs a health endpoint.

patterns.name: Mock Object for External Dependency
patterns.summary: A mock client provides deterministic responses for tests or offline usage.
patterns.intent: To isolate the system from external LLM services during development and testing.
patterns.context: The system relies on external LLM calls that are non-deterministic and costly.
forces: Tests should not depend on network or API availability
Need for reproducible test fixtures
Allow offline development
patterns.solution: Create a MockLLMClient that returns canned responses according to some simple heuristics.

costs: Mock behavior may drift from real provider
Requires maintenance to stay in sync
failure_modes: If mock responses are too limited, tests may pass but production fail.

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard practice for any external API client.

anti_patterns.name: Missing Explicit Interfaces for LLM Clients
symptoms: No abstract base class or Protocol visible for LLM clients
Reliance on duck typing may lead to mismatches
impact: Can make it difficult to enforce consistent contract across providers
Heavier refactoring when adding new providers
suggested_remediation: Introduce an abstract base class (ABC) or Protocol for LLM client methods
Define common methods and type hints

anti_patterns.name: Potential God Object in Governance Models
symptoms: Many model classes defined in a single models.py file
May become a dumping ground for all domain schemas
impact: File can become too large and hard to maintain
Changes in one model may affect many others
suggested_remediation: Split models into separate modules by aggregate or bounded context
Consider using separate namespaces per domain concept

cross_cutting_concerns.description: GovernanceException and likely other exceptions to handle domain errors; also validation via Pydantic.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Configuration Management
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Bootstrap functions manage merging and copying configuration files; pyproject.toml centralizes package metadata.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Validation
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Pydantic is used for domain models and likely for input validation; jsonschema dependency for schema validation.
